title: Lisse coefficients on an open relative affine line over an integer model
statement: Let $\Lambda$ be a finite commutative ring. Work in the bounded-below derived categories of sheaves of $\Lambda$-modules on small etale sites [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories] [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. For any separated finite-type morphism $h:T\to B$ of quasi-compact and quasi-separated schemes [def-pc-scheme] [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], a compactification $c=(j:T\hookrightarrow\overline T,p:\overline T\to B)$ consists of a quasi-compact open immersion $j$ and a proper morphism $p$ with $h=pj$ [def-weil-pbc-projection-compactification]; write $Rh_!^c=Rp_*j_!$ [def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero]. Let $Y=\operatorname{Spec}R$ for a finitely generated $\mathbf Z$-algebra $R$ (a commutative ring generated by finitely many elements as a ring). Let $U\subseteq\mathbf A^1_Y$ be an open subscheme [def-nagata-relative-affine-space], let $f:U\to Y$ be the restricted projection, and let $L$ be a sheaf of $\Lambda$-modules on $U_{\Et}$ locally isomorphic on an etale cover to constant sheaves of finite $\Lambda$-modules [def-constructible-locally-constant] [def-weil-pbc-etale-constructible-sheaf]. Regard $L$ as a complex in degree zero. For every compactification $c$ of $f$ and every $q\in\mathbf Z$, $\mathcal H^q(Rf_!^cL)$ is constructible on $Y_{\Et}$ [def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves].

source.place: Tag 0GKY, label lemma-loc-constant-shriek-rel-dim-1; specialization to finite rings and affine finite-type integer bases

proof.text: By finite-type-over-Noetherian, $Y$ and $\mathbf A^1_Y$ are Noetherian. Their affine coordinate rings are Noetherian, so the affine-Noetherian underlying-space theorem makes $\mathbf A^1_Y$ a Noetherian topological space. Every open in such a space is quasi-compact: otherwise finite unions from a covering have no maximal member, contradicting ascending-chain termination for opens. Choose a finite principal cover $U=\bigcup_{i=1}^rD(s_i)$ inside $\operatorname{Spec}R[t]$. Every finite intersection is again principal, $D(s_{i_1}\cdots s_{i_k})$, hence affine. It is smooth of relative dimension one over $Y$: affine-space smoothness gives the projection, and restriction through a principal open preserves it by smooth-relative-dimension permanence. Here $D(s)\to\operatorname{Spec}B$ is smooth of relative dimension zero directly from the smooth definition: $B_s=B[v]/(sv-1)$ is finitely presented, and $s$ invertible modulo a square-zero ideal stays invertible, since $(1+i)^{-1}=1-i$ when $i^2=0$, so every infinitesimal lifting uniquely factors through the localization. Its nonempty fibres are open subschemes of a point, hence dimension zero. The empty open has zero image and needs no argument. It remains to prove the assertion for every such principal open, then glue by relative Mayer--Vietoris.

source.place: Tag 0GKY; affine-cover expansion required to apply 0GKX

proof.text: Fix a principal open $W$ and write $h:W\to Y$. Let $N>0$ annihilate the additive group of the finite ring $\Lambda$ and factor $N=\prod_\ell\ell^{n_\ell}$. Choose integers $e_\ell$ which are 1 modulo $\ell^{n_\ell}$ and 0 modulo the other factors (Bezout gives these residues). Multiplication by $e_\ell$ defines pairwise orthogonal idempotents on $L|_W$ with sum 1, so $L|_W=\bigoplus_\ell F_\ell$, each $\ell^{n_\ell}F_\ell=0$. These are finite locally constant $\Lambda$-module sheaves: on any constant trivializing cover, take the same idempotent summands of the finite fibre module. A derived additive functor preserves this finite split sum, so it suffices to treat one $F=F_\ell$. The zero-ring/zero-sheaf case is already zero.

Apply the prime-to-primary filtration cover input to the affine Noetherian $W$ and $F$. It gives $g:T\to W$, affine clopen components $T_a$, filtrations by constant finite modules on each $T_a$, and constant fibre cardinality $d$ prime to $\ell$. The module trace-degree theorem gives a $\Lambda$-linear $t:g_*g^{-1}F\to F$ with $t\eta=d\,\mathrm{id}_F$. Choose an integer $a$ with $ad\equiv1\pmod{\ell^n}$; since $\ell^nF=0$, the map $at$ retracts $\eta$. Finite direct-image exactness for abelian sheaves implies exactness for these module sheaves too: the underlying direct image is the abelian direct image and a sequence of module sheaves is exact exactly when its underlying abelian sequence is exact. Using the module direct-image construction, take an injective resolution of a degree-zero module sheaf. Exactness makes its termwise direct image a resolution of its direct image, so the computation of derived direct image gives $Rg_*=g_*$ on degree-zero sheaves. Choose a compactification of $hg$ by Nagata: $T$ is finite over the affine $W$, hence affine and quasi-compact and quasi-separated, and $hg$ is separated of finite type over the affine $Y$. A finite morphism is proper, so the identity compactification gives $Rg_!=Rg_*$. Shriek composition and compactification independence identify $Rh_!g_*g^{-1}F\cong R(hg)_!g^{-1}F$. Applying the additive $Rh_!$ to the split maps shows $Rh_!F$ is a retract of this latter object, hence each of its cohomology sheaves is a retract as well.

For a chosen compactification $c=(j,p)$, exactness of module extension by zero and the exact-functor derived theorem make $j_!$ triangulated. Module direct image is additive left exact and its source has enough injectives, so the right-derived theorem makes $Rp_*$ triangulated. Thus $Rp_*j_!$ is additive and triangulated: apply the two functors successively to a distinguished triangle and compose their shift isomorphisms. This applies to every compactification used below.

proof.text: Put $k_a=hg|_{T_a}:T_a\to Y$. The cover input makes $T_a$ affine and $g|_{T_a}$ etale. Since $W$ and $Y$ are affine, $h$ is affine; an affine morphism has affine inverse images of all affine opens, and a morphism between affine schemes is affine (localize the corresponding ring map). Affine morphisms are separated and quasi-compact by affine permanence. Smooth-relative-dimension permanence gives $k_a$ smooth of relative dimension $0+1=1$. It is finite type: $h$ is finitely presented, and $g|_{T_a}$ is finite, as a clopen summand of the finite cover (on rings, it is an idempotent summand of a finite module). Nagata supplies a compactification of $k_a$. Apply the constant-coefficient relative-dimension-one theorem to every constant quotient $Q_{a,i}$ in the cover input; every $H^q(R(k_a)_!Q_{a,i})$ is constructible.

proof.text: Apply finite-filtration devissage to $\Phi=R(k_a)_!$, the filtration $F_{a,i}$ supplied in step 3, and the class of constructible $\Lambda$-module sheaves on $Y_{\Et}$. This class contains zero by its definition and is closed under kernels, cokernels and extensions by the constructible Serre theorem. The preceding step verifies the hypothesis for every quotient and every degree, and the first replacement step verifies that $\Phi$ is triangulated. We obtain constructibility of every $H^q(R(k_a)_!(g^{-1}F|_{T_a}))$.

proof.text: Write $i_a:T_a\hookrightarrow T$. Apply the disjoint-open-extension biproduct theorem to the finite disjoint open cover of $T$ and $G=g^{-1}F$: $G\cong\bigoplus_a i_{a!}(G|_{T_a})$. Each $i_a$ has compactification $(i_a,\mathrm{id}_T)$, so its candidate shriek is the exact $i_{a!}$. Additivity of $R(hg)_!$ preserves this finite biproduct, and shriek composition identifies its $a$-th image with $R(k_a)_!(G|_{T_a})$. Thus $R(hg)_!G\cong\bigoplus_a R(k_a)_!(G|_{T_a})$. Applying cohomology preserves the biproduct relations, so every cohomology sheaf is the finite sum of the constructible component cohomology sheaves. A finite sum of constructible sheaves is constructible by repeated extension closure applied to $0\to A\to A\oplus B\to B\to0$.

source.place: Tag 0GKY final sentence invoking Tag 0GKX; Tag 03RZ filtration and retract closure

proof.text: Step 3 gives a retract on every cohomology sheaf: write $s:A\to B$ and $r:B\to A$ with $rs=1_A$, where $B$ is the constructible sheaf just obtained. Put $e=sr$. The map $s$ identifies $A$ with $\ker(1_B-e)$: $(1-e)s=0$, and if $(1-e)b=0$ then $b=s(rb)$, with inverse the restriction of $r$. Kernel closure for the endomorphism $1-e$ of the constructible $B$ therefore proves $A$ constructible. Finally, the primary decomposition of step 2 is a finite split sum; additivity and repeated Serre extension closure give constructibility of $Rh_!(L|_W)$ in all degrees, for every chosen compactification.

proof.text: Induct on the number of principal opens covering $U$. The one-open case is steps 4--8. For $U=W_1\cup V$ with $V$ the union of the remaining opens, the intersection $W_1\cap V$ is covered by the at most $r-1$ principal opens $W_1\cap W_i$; all their finite intersections remain principal. The induction hypothesis applies both to $V$ and to $W_1\cap V$, with the restricted sheaf. The restricted maps are separated of finite type: the opens are quasi-compact in the Noetherian $U$, and their affine principal covers have finitely presented coordinate algebras over $R$. Choose their compactifications by Nagata. Relative Mayer--Vietoris for these quasi-compact opens gives a triangle $R(W_1\cap V\to Y)_!L\to R(W_1\to Y)_!L\oplus R(V\to Y)_!L\to Rf_!^cL\to$. In its cohomology sequence the third term is an extension of a cokernel and a kernel involving cohomology of the first two terms. Serre closure proves it constructible in every degree. The relative Mayer--Vietoris statement is for arbitrary chosen compactifications, so this proves the required assertion for the given $c$ without changing the candidate shriek.
